problem: Existing visual-audio navigation (VAN) methods such as AV-Nav and AV-Wan generalize poorly to unheard sound categories (SR drops from ~90% to ~50% on Replica) and are sample inefficient (3M-13M steps with pure RL losses).
motivation: Real deployments (e.g. guard robots) face sounds not seen in training. Human hearing separates 'what' (semantic) from 'where' (spatial) pathways, and spatial cues stay invariant across sound categories, so semantic information should be suppressed and spatial information emphasized.
key_idea: Add two plug-and-play auxiliary tasks: adversarial sound-category classification via a gradient reversal layer to make the audio features semantic-agnostic, and sound direction (yaw/pitch) prediction to make the features spatial-aware.
insight: Both components are needed. In the ablations (Table 3), removing the audio classifier (AC) or the location predictor (LP) each lowers performance; e.g. Replica AV-Nav SR falls from 0.823 to 0.749 without AC and 0.766 without LP, and to 0.576 without both. LP matters more on the larger MP3D scenes. The paper argues LP is also needed so the adversarial task does not collapse the encoder into ignoring spatial information. The gain is mainly on unheard categories, with heard categories roughly unchanged.
method: Semantic-Agnostic Learning: a 4-layer FC audio classifier (AC) predicts the sound category from audio features; a gradient reversal layer multiplies the gradient into the audio encoder by -λ, so the encoder learns to remove category information.
Adversarial intensity schedule: λ = 2b/(1+exp(-10 n/N)) - b, growing with completed episodes n out of N, bounded by b.

Spatial-Aware Learning: a 4-layer FC location predictor (LP) takes temporal features from the time-series model over visual and audio encodings and regresses sin/cos of the relative yaw α and pitch β of the sound source, using an MSE loss.
Joint training: the LP gradients update the audio encoder, visual encoder and time-series model; the AC updates only θ_C and adversarially the audio encoder; everything is trained jointly with PPO.

Plug-and-play backbones: applied unchanged to AV-Nav (end-to-end) and AV-Wan (waypoint plus acoustic/geometric map), following their reward designs (+10 on Stop at the goal, distance-based shaping, -0.01 per step).

setting.backbone: AV-Nav and AV-Wan (RL policies, trained from scratch) with the added AC and LP heads
setting.training_data: SoundSpaces Replica (9 train scenes) and MP3D (57 train scenes), 73 heard training sound categories; no extra data. Evaluated on unheard categories (18 test).
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph moves: MoveForward, TurnLeft, TurnRight, Stop (150 steps per episode)
setting.privileged: GT sound direction and sound category labels are used as training-time supervision only; none at test time (AV-Wan builds its own maps)

numbers.extra: unheard sound categories, zero-shot to unseen scenes

numbers_note: The benchmark is SoundSpaces AudioGoal navigation, which is not in the canonical list, so it is recorded as other:. The split is the test scenes (Replica 5, MP3D 12) with heard and unheard sound categories. Noise-robustness results (SPL under SNR 20-50, with and without depth noise) are in Table 3 and not listed here.
results: Applied to AV-Nav and AV-Wan, the method greatly improves unheard-category performance: Replica AV-Nav SR 0.576→0.823 and SPL 0.394→0.606; AV-Wan SR 0.424→0.628; MP3D AV-Nav SR 0.359→0.602. Heard-category performance is mostly maintained (Replica AV-Nav SR is slightly lower at 0.898 vs 0.903; MP3D AV-Nav SR is lower at 0.652 vs 0.700). Learning curves show it surpasses the baseline's best SPL with fewer training samples, and it stays robust under audio and depth noise.
limitations: Simulation only; sim2real transfer for audio and vision is not tested.
Single static sound source only; multiple or moving sources are left as future work.
Some heard-category metrics dropped slightly (MP3D AV-Nav SR 0.700→0.652), and the gains rely on category labels and GT direction for auxiliary supervision.
